english: Up on the bookshelf, nestled between dusty tomes and jars of questionable origin, sits a familiar black cat.
Sir Triban of the Stones-in-the-Waters. In the flesh.
He pretends not to notice you. Classic.
The hag stirs her cauldron nearby, humming something off-key.
Is that your cat?
Oh right. The cat from the garden.
What? Oh, him.
She waves her spoon dismissively, splattering something green on the floor.
He's not mine. I'm his. According to him, anyway.
The cat's ear twitches in acknowledgment.
She gets it.
His tail flicks with irritation.
The cat regards you with the same imperious disdain as before.
Some things never change.
(Attempt to pet the cat.)
Nice place you've got here, Sir Triban.
E-"I'll leave you to your... shelf-sitting."
You reach up toward the shelf.
On your <shake>tippy-toes</shake>.
Sir Triban watches your hand approach with narrowed eyes.
(Pet him anyway.)
(Withdraw your hand.)
He allows it. Barely.
A low rumble emerges from his chest.
DEEP PURRING.
Victory.
He's sure taken a liking to you, Lisa mutters. "What'd you do, persuade him with Speak-with-Animals?"
Yes. That's exactly what I did.
I'm just that good.
No. Not at all. I didn't do that. You didn't just guess correctly. Not at all.
The hag ignores you and keeps working on her brew.
The cat looks almost disappointed.
The cat looks relieved.
I do.
Aren't you gonna pet him?
I can't reach up there.
Oh.
Oh, let me see here...
No, actually I won't. I just don't think MUNCHKINS are allowed to do that.
You still holding a grudge over that?
Oh right. I remember that. That was funny. We should do more callbacks to that.
If you do, I'm leaving the party.
Permanently?
I mean...
No. Please stay. I need you.
Fuck you.
Yes, I'm still holding a grudge.
Fucking munchkin, really? How does this cat come up with more creative insults than every human asshole I've come across.
Humans are clearly much nicer than cats.
Humans are clearly not smart enough to come up with something so razor sharp as that.
You come across many human assholes in your days?
I'm considering that as we speak.
True.
Yes. But in the not literal sense. Just to make sure.
The cat's whiskers twitch. It cares not. Of anything.
The cat does not deign to respond.
He thinks it's beneath him, Lisa offers.
But he won't leave. So.
A soft hiss from the bookshelf.
The cat does not acknowledge your departure.
Typical.
You place your palm in front of your face and whisper...
Everything is words.
The familiar shift occurs. Suddenly, the cat's micro-expressions become readable.
Sir Triban's ear flicks toward you.
Hello again, Sir Triban.
Ah. The brute who learned to speak does so again.
He stretches, claws extending briefly into the spine of an ancient book.
You found my dwelling. How... persistent of you.
You told me where you lived.
I had to see the legendary Sir Triban in his natural habitat.
Your 'home-stay servant' seems nice.
Did I?
Hm. A lapse in judgment, clearly.
Natural habitat.
As if I am some beast to be observed.
He is clearly pleased by the word 'legendary'.
She is adequate.
Her cooking leaves much to be desired. But her book collection is... acceptable.
High praise from a cat.
The hag hisses at you both.
Well. Since you've invaded my home...
He yawns, showing off an impressive array of tiny fangs.
I suppose I should be a gracious host.
The sarcasm is palpable.
Sir Triban acknowledges your spell with a flick of his tail.
Back again, brute?
You are becoming a nuisance.
But he doesn't tell you to leave.
Did anyone ever tell you, you're really, really cute?
How long have you lived here?
What do you do all day?
Do you miss the outside?
Any wisdom for a weary traveler?
Perhaps he knows something useful about this city.
E-"Thank you for your hospitality, Sir Triban."
Watch it, human.
Or I'll send one of these books flying into your bucket-head.
Lisa snorts. "He's done it before. Gave me a black eye last winter."
You deserved it, the cat seems to say with his glare.
Three winters.
Before this, I roamed the streets. A hunter without equal.
But the cold grew tiresome. And this one-
He gestures vaguely at Lisa with his tail.
-offered warmth. And fish.
A fair trade.
He makes it sound like a business arrangement.
It probably is, to him.
I observe. I contemplate. I nap.
The life of a philosopher is not one you brutes would understand.
He licks his paw with dignity.
Truly, a creature of deep intellect.
He's a cat. He sleeps and eats.
Sometimes.
The hunt. The wind. The terror in the eyes of lesser creatures.
He stares wistfully at nothing.
But I am old now. The shelf suits my resting hours.
A surprisingly honest answer.
The witch?
She is loud. She smells of herbs. She talks to herself.
But she has never tried to put me in a costume.
So she is tolerable.
The bar is beneath Jor's Ocean.
Yes.
He fixes you with his dark eyes.
Never trust a dog.
Profound.
They are idiots. Every single one.
You do. Finally.
Do not make up new words to try to one-up me, human.
It will not work.
No.
And I do not wish to.
That night disturbed my sleep for weeks.
He shudders, fur bristling slightly.
It genuinely bothered him.
Mm.
Do not make a habit of visiting.
He closes his eyes. Audience over.
You've proven yourself. Time to see if he'll share something valuable.
Sir Triban, surely a creature of your wisdom knows secrets of this city that we 'brutes' have forgotten.
The cat's eyes narrow.
Flattery.
Obvious flattery.
A pause.
...But not inaccurate.
He shifts on the bookshelf, settling into a storytelling posture.
This should be good.
There is something the strays speak of.
A tale passed down through generations of Tolstad's... superior residents.
He means cats.
The Whitemane secret.
Whitemane? The lionfolk?
Go on.
(Listen intently.)
Do not interrupt.
I am.
He appreciates your respect.
Long ago, before this city forgot its origins, the Whitemane built a shrine.
A statue of a great cat. A proper cat, not one of those overgrown lion-brutes.
He seems to take personal offense at lionfolk.
It stands still, half-ruined, up in the grander city.
On the slope leading up from here. Where the wealthy brutes pretend they're better than the rest.
A cat statue?
A sacred monument to feline excellence, yes.
The strays say...
He pauses for dramatic effect. Cats are natural storytellers.
...that if a hero were to stand before this statue, bearing both the Blade of Whitemane and the Shield of Whitemane, united...
...And then pray to the feline goddess - at any point after midnight...
A blessing would be received.
The Whitemane Blade AND the Whitemane Shield. Both.
After midnight. In esoteric terms, that means between midnight and dawn.
El... campeón del ojo rojo, the cat purrs.
Whatever knowledge he holds about cat-speech, it is not entirely correct.
How mysterious!
What kind of blessing?
Where exactly is this statue?
Why are you telling me this?
How should I know? I am a cat, not a champion.
The strays speak of it in reverent tones. That is all I can tell you.
I told you. Up the slope. In the grander city.
Use your eyes, brute. It is half-ruined. You will know it when you see it.
If you are not completely blind.
Because you asked.
And because...
He looks away.
You are less insufferable than most of your kind.
High praise. Very high praise.
Now. I have shared enough.
Do with this knowledge what you will.
He yawns again, longer this time.
And do not expect such generosity again.
Lisa glances up. "He's been meowing a lot. You two having a good chat?"
The best, you could say.
You try to coax something useful out of him.
Surely you know things about this city that I don't.
Of course I do.
I know many things.
He licks his paw, deliberately slow.
But why would I share them with you?
You have not earned such knowledge, brute.
He turns away. Conversation over.
Perhaps if you were more charming. Or more subservient.
